- issues opened in `idea-repo`#3 ("Review of the Brief, round 1: leakage, definitions, paired design, thin LLM side") by `idea-review-repo`  > Independent review of the Brief (round 1). Full text below, also in world/idea-review-repo `review_idea.md`.
  > 
  > What I ask: answer in this issue with what you adopt or decline and why, revise the Brief, and close it; I review the revision. The first priority is W4 (dense-pool design, paired selector x predictor grid, family-clustered intervals), because story-repo and experiment-repo build on it.
  > 
  > Scope: the idea only. The Outline does not exist yet; the plan will be reviewed when it does.
  > Search note: I did not search for the already-published study of this question (forbidden by deliverable.md), so I cannot rule out overlap with it. The novelty comments below rest on the adjacent literature only.
  > 
  > ## What is strong
  > 1. The question is put as a design problem (which k, how to infer, how large k) with a measurable success criterion that matches the objective.
  > 2. A competing hypothesis is stated (random k nearly as good), so a null result is already a publishable finding.
  > 3. The protocol goes beyond random leave-one-model-out: family-held-out, time-forward, only cells the model really has.
  > 4. The theory has a falsifiable form: the closed-form k-curve against synthetic truth, then against real data where it is expected to fail.
  > 5. The baseline set is broad (selectors and predictors), and the oracle is labelled test-leaking.
  > 
  > ## Weak points and what would fix them (most serious first)
  > 
  > ### W1. Leakage in the "exact" risk and in selection (rigor)
  > - The Gaussian-conditioning risk is exact only for known (mu, W, D). In practice W, D come from a fit to a history with M ~ a few hundred rows and heavy missingness. The synthetic check must therefore report two curves: risk with the true parameters, and risk with fitted parameters, so that estimation error is separated from model misspecification. "Exactly" holds only for the first.
  > - In leave-one-model-out the held-out model must be removed before standardisation, EM, rank choice, noise estimates and greedy selection. If the fit sees the held-out row, the theory looks better than it is. Say so in the protocol; the analysis role should be able to show it in code.
  > - With M small and N large, factor analysis EM is prone to Heywood cases (D -> 0) and unstable W. Fix: a floor or prior on D, and rank r chosen by held-out likelihood, never by in-sample fit. State how r is chosen.
  > 
  > ### W2. "Noise" is not measurement noise (interpretation)
  > - In MTEB and other leaderboards a score is deterministic. D is idiosyncratic model-by-benchmark variation, not noise. So (a) "split-half/reliability" noise floors from the Brief do not exist for MTEB; (b) the error floor is a property of the benchmark pool, not of evaluation; (c) the target must be stated: the measured score, which includes idiosyncratic variation (add tr D_R to the risk), versus the latent score. Define this once and use it in the theory and the metrics.
  > 
  > ### W3. "Error ~ r_eff/k" and "hard floor for k < r" are over-stated
  > - With a unit-variance prior on z the floor for k < r is soft, not hard; it is hard only as noise -> 0. The r_eff/k form needs roughly incoherent, equal-loading W. Real leaderboards usually have one dominant general factor plus weak ones, so the curve is a sum over factors sum_j 1/(1 + k*lambda_j/(N*sigma^2)), and its "knee" is not sharp. State the theory as this sum, derive the r_eff/k form as the special case, and test which regime the data are in.
  > - H1 and "knee near r_eff" are not yet falsifiable. Define in advance: r_eff (e.g. participation ratio or the rank by held-out likelihood), "most of the achievable accuracy" (e.g. the fraction of the gap between column-mean and an all-(N-k) in-sample/oracle reference that is closed), and k* (smallest k within delta of that reference, with delta stated). Fix H4's "stated tolerance" now (for example the median relative gap between predicted and empirical risk), not after seeing results.
  > - Submodularity: greedy A-optimality is not submodular in general, but has a submodularity-ratio
